ui.faqIntro: Straight answers about travelling with KiwiCamping.
ui.faq1a: KiwiCamping is an iPhone app for finding places to camp and stay around New Zealand. It bundles a directory of 6,500+ places so the details stay readable without reception, and it turns the ones you save into a road trip with an ordered route, dates, notes and to-dos.
ui.faq2a: More than 6,500 places: DOC campsites, backcountry huts, holiday parks and other bookable stays, freedom camping areas, public dump stations and day-use places across both islands.
ui.faq3a: The place directory is bundled with the app, so names, categories, descriptions, fees, facilities and conditions stay readable well beyond signal. Live services such as weather, routing, Look Around imagery, photos and provider pages still need a connection.
ui.faq4q: Can I plan a multi-stop road trip?
ui.faq4a: Yes, and it is the app's main feature. Add places as stops, drag them into order, attach a date and arrival notes to each one, see the driving distance leg by leg and across the whole trip, open directions to the next stop, check the weather at each one, tick stops off as visited and keep the packing list beside the itinerary. Itinerary details can sync to Calendar.
ui.faq5a: Two kinds. Smart collections (Liked, Starred, Want to visit, Visited, Pins and All saved) fill themselves as you mark places. On top of those you can create your own named collections with an icon and notes for a region, a season, a vehicle or a shortlist.
ui.faq6q: Can I filter for free camps or self-contained sites?
ui.faq6a: Yes, and combinations of them. Filters cover place type, fee, minimum rating, online booking, region and detailed facility and access features, so “free camping areas with toilets and drinking water near Queenstown” is a single query.
ui.faq7q: What is on a place screen?
ui.faq7a: Photos, a description, opening hours, fees, terms and conditions, facilities grouped by type, current alerts, ratings, contact and booking details, weather, Look Around where coverage exists, directions, and nearby alternatives.
ui.faq8a: A standard map and a satellite view built on Apple's flyover imagery, which you can tilt and rotate for real 3D terrain. Apple Look Around gives the street-level view from the place screen.
ui.faq9q: Can I see prices in my own currency?
ui.faq9a: Yes. Choose your currency in settings and set the conversion rate, and reported costs are shown in that currency alongside the New Zealand dollar figure.
ui.faq10q: Can I book a campsite in KiwiCamping?
ui.faq10a: Open the booking details for a place to reach its provider and check live availability, prices and terms.
ui.faq11q: Are camping rules the same across New Zealand?
ui.faq11a: No. National law, council bylaws, conservation rules and individual site conditions can all apply. Always follow current signs, land-manager directions, fire restrictions and official alerts.

sections.heading: Finding places
paragraphs: Search by place name, address or description. Move the map and choose the current-area option to focus results around the visible region.
Filter by place type, fee, minimum rating, online booking, region and detailed facility and access features. Combine only the filters that matter so useful alternatives remain visible.
Facilities, fees, access and management can change. Follow current signs and the land manager, then send a correction so the directory can improve.

sections.heading: Saved places
paragraphs: Liked, Visited, Want to Visit and Starred update automatically when you mark places. Pins and All Saved provide other quick views.
Create named collections with an icon and notes, then add any place. Use them for a region, season, vehicle or shortlist.
The app supports private iCloud sync for saved states, collections and trip data when iCloud is available and enabled.

sections.heading: Trip planner
paragraphs: Create a trip, add places and drag them into order. Each stop can carry its own arrival date, notes, weather and visited status, and the planner shows the driving distance leg by leg and across the whole trip.
Road routing depends on available MapKit directions. The planner retains the stops if a leg fails, but you must confirm current road access yourself.
Start with a camping essentials preset or make your own tasks. Trip progress keeps the list beside the itinerary, and itinerary details can sync to Calendar.

sections.heading: Maps, weather and live details
paragraphs: Switch between the standard map and a satellite view built on Apple's flyover imagery, which tilts and rotates into 3D terrain. Apple Look Around, the street-level view, opens from the place screen where coverage exists.
Current and forecast weather requires live data. Save critical forecasts and official warnings before leaving coverage.
The bundled place directory keeps core place details available beyond reliable signal. Live maps, routing, weather, photos and external provider pages may require reception.

sections.heading: Prices and currency
paragraphs: Choose your currency in settings and set the conversion rate. Reported costs are then shown in that currency alongside the New Zealand dollar figure, which helps when you are visiting and not fluent in NZD.
Open a place's booking or contact details to check availability, price and terms with the provider. Prices in the app are reported figures, not live quotes.

sections.heading: Premium and purchases

Premium adds unlimited saved lists, trip planning, advanced filters, place weather and road trip routes.
Use Restore Purchases on the Premium screen while signed into the Apple account used for the original transaction.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lede: KiwiCamping helps you plan a trip without turning your journey into an advertising profile.

sections.heading: Information stored on your device
paragraphs: Saved places, collection membership, trips, notes, checklist items and preferences are stored for the app to work. Location can be used to show your position and nearby places after you grant permission.

sections.heading: iCloud
paragraphs: When iCloud is available and enabled, the app can use your private iCloud database to sync saved states, collections and app records across your devices. Apple provides the underlying service and applies its own terms.

sections.heading: Live Apple services
paragraphs: Map display, directions, Look Around, weather, calendar integration and widgets may use Apple frameworks. Requests and data handling for those services are governed by Apple. Calendar access occurs only after permission and is used to add trip itinerary information you request.

sections.heading: External links and website logs
paragraphs: Place details can open booking providers, websites, social profiles, phone numbers, email addresses and map apps. Those services receive information according to their own policies when you choose to open them.

Hosting providers may process routine technical logs such as IP address, browser type and requested URL for delivery, reliability and security. KiwiCamping does not use advertising trackers on this website.

sections.heading: Website analytics
paragraphs: This website uses Google Analytics 4 to count visits and to see which pages lead people to the App Store. Google processes this data on our behalf as a processor. For visitors in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland the service is provided by Google Ireland Limited, and elsewhere by Google LLC.

Analytics records the pages you view, your device, browser and screen type, an approximate location derived from your IP address (Google does not store the address itself), the page that sent you here and your clicks on App Store links. It never receives your name, your email address or anything you save in the app.

When analytics is allowed, Google Analytics sets two first-party cookies: _ga, and a second whose name starts with _ga_. Both expire after 13 months. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland these cookies are set only after you choose Accept on the consent bar. Until then, and if you choose Decline, no analytics cookies are stored and Google receives only cookieless signals that carry no identifier. You can change your choice at any time with the Privacy choices link at the foot of every page.

Google signals and ad personalisation are switched off, so analytics data is not linked to Google accounts and is not used for advertising. Analytics data is kept for 14 months and then deleted. KiwiCamping still uses no advertising trackers on this website.

sections.heading: Retention and control
paragraphs: You can delete app records through the app and manage iCloud data through your Apple account. Removing the app can remove local data, while synced copies may remain in iCloud until separately deleted.

sections.heading: Children and contact
paragraphs: KiwiCamping is a general travel utility and is not directed to children. Do not submit personal information about a child through support.
For privacy questions, contact KiwiCamping support.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lede: KiwiCamping is a planning aid. It does not replace official signs, land-manager directions, emergency warnings, road advice or your responsibility to travel within your capability.

sections.heading: Travel information changes
paragraphs: Places, prices, access, facilities, phone coverage, weather, fire conditions, roads and booking arrangements can change without notice. Verify critical details with the responsible authority or provider before travel and again close to departure.

sections.heading: No booking or access guarantee
paragraphs: A listing does not guarantee that a place is open, legal for your setup, reachable by your vehicle or available. External booking and contact links are provided for convenience. Contracts are between you and the third-party provider.

sections.heading: Safety and lawful use
paragraphs: You must obey signs, permits, closures, fire restrictions, road rules and directions from rangers, iwi, hapū, emergency services and land managers. Do not use the app while driving.

sections.heading: User data
paragraphs: You are responsible for notes, trip plans and other information you save. Keep separate copies of permits, bookings and safety-critical plans when loss of access could put a trip at risk.

sections.heading: Purchases
paragraphs: Any in-app purchase is processed by Apple and subject to the terms shown at purchase. Features, packaging and prices may change where allowed. Use Apple’s purchase tools for billing, cancellation and refund matters.

fuel.metaTitle: Fuel Cost Calculator NZ: Campervan Road Trip Fuel
fuel.metaDescription: Work out litres and fuel cost for a New Zealand road trip from distance, L/100 km and the pump price, with the formula, a 1,000 km worked example and MBIE's benchmark.
fuel.h1: Fuel cost calculator for a New Zealand road trip
fuel.intro: Enter the route distance, your vehicle's loaded fuel use and the price per litre. The default price is MBIE's national board price for regular 91 petrol in the week ending 26 July 2026.
fuel.cardText: Enter the full route distance, the vehicle's loaded fuel use and the expected price per litre. Remote prices can exceed city benchmarks.
fuel.formulaNote: Consumption is quoted per 100 kilometres, so dividing by 100 turns it into litres per kilometre. The sum is linear: double the distance and both the litres and the cost double.
fuel.example: A {distance} km route in a campervan using {consumption} L/100 km needs {litres} litres of fuel. At {price} a litre, that is {cost}.
assumptions: The default price is a national benchmark. Remote stations, including on the West Coast and in Fiordland, often charge more, so fill up before long gaps between towns.
Use the loaded consumption of the vehicle you are actually driving. A full campervan on hills and into a headwind uses more than its brochure figure.
Add the local driving around each stop. Supermarket runs, viewpoints and side roads add up over a long route.
Diesel vehicles pay road user charges (RUC) for every 1,000 km on top of fuel. This calculator covers fuel only.
faq: How much fuel does a campervan use in New Zealand?

It depends on the vehicle, the load and the roads. Use the figure from your hire company or vehicle and allow a margin for hills. The 12 L/100 km default is a planning figure for a loaded campervan, not a measured average.
Does the fuel cost include road user charges?
No. Diesel vehicles in New Zealand pay road user charges per 1,000 km separately from fuel. Ask your hire company whether RUC is included in the rate, and check NZTA for current charges.
Where does the default fuel price come from?
It is MBIE's national board price for regular 91 petrol in the week ending 26 July 2026. MBIE publishes fuel prices every week, so check the latest figure before you go.

drive.metaTitle: Driving Time Calculator NZ: Realistic Hours by Road Type
drive.metaDescription: Estimate how long a New Zealand driving day really takes from the distance, the kind of road and your stops, with the formula, a worked example and the speeds used.
drive.h1: Driving time calculator for New Zealand roads
drive.intro: Routing apps give moving time on an ideal road. This calculator takes the distance you already know, an average speed for the kind of road and 20 minutes for every stop, which is where a New Zealand driving day usually runs over.
drive.cardTitle: How long that day really takes.
drive.cardText: Routing apps give moving time on an ideal road. This adds the road character and your actual stops, which is where a day usually runs over.
drive.formulaNote: The average speed is not the speed limit. It allows for corners, hills, one-lane bridges, towns and slower traffic. The four road types use 85, 70, 60 and 45 km/h.
drive.example: A {distance} km day on winding or coastal roads at {speed} km/h is {driving} of driving. Add {stops} stops at 20 minutes each and the day takes {total}.
assumptions: The average speeds are planning figures for a car or campervan in good conditions, not measured averages for any one road.
Each stop counts 20 minutes for fuel, food, a toilet or a viewpoint. Ferries, road works and long walks need adding on top.
Weather, slips and closures change routes. Check NZTA's journey planner for current road conditions before you set off.
faq: How far can you drive in a day in New Zealand?

There is no single number. Winding roads, one-lane bridges and stops keep average speeds well below the open-road limit, so a day that looks short on a map can take most of the daylight. Enter the distance and road type to see the hours, and plan regular rest breaks.
Why is this longer than my maps app?
Maps apps estimate moving time with no stops. This uses an average for the kind of road and adds time for each stop, which is closer to how a camping day actually goes.
Does it work for a campervan?
Yes. Choose a slower road type if you are driving a large vehicle, towing, or new to driving on the left.

campsite.metaTitle: Campsite Cost Calculator NZ: Per Person or Per Site?
campsite.metaDescription: Compare a DOC campsite charged per adult with a holiday park charged per site for your group and nights, with the formula, a worked example and DOC fee figures from the data.
campsite.h1: Campsite cost calculator: per person or per site
campsite.intro: DOC campsites charge per adult per night, while a holiday park usually charges per site. Which one is cheaper flips with the size of your group, and this works it out for your nights.
campsite.cardText: A DOC campsite usually charges per adult and a holiday park usually charges per site. The cheaper option flips with party size, which catches families out.
formula: Per-adult total = adults × nights × rate per adult
Per-site total = nights × rate per site
The lower total is the cheaper option for your group
campsite.formulaNote: The per-adult total grows with every extra adult, while the per-site total does not. That is why the answer changes between a couple and a family.
campsite.example: {adults} adults staying {nights} nights at {rateAdult} per adult pay {totalAdult}. The same stay at {rateSite} per site costs {totalSite}, so {verdict}.
assumptions: Children are left out. Many DOC campsites charge a reduced rate for ages 5 to 17 and nothing for infants, and holiday parks set their own child rates.
The default rates are examples, not quotes. In the DOC data as of {docDate}, {docFree} DOC campsites are free, and the lowest adult rate listed at paid ones runs from {docMin} to {docMax} per night.
Holiday parks set their own prices, which change with the season, power and site size. Check the park before you book.
faq: How much does a campsite cost per night in New Zealand?

DOC campsites are either free or charge per adult. In the DOC data as of {docDate}, the lowest adult rate at paid DOC campsites runs from {docMin} to {docMax} per night, with a median of {docMedian}. Holiday parks set their own site prices, so compare the total for your group.
Is per person or per site cheaper for a family?
Per site usually wins as the group grows, because the site price stays the same while per-adult charges multiply. Enter your own rates to see where the break-even point falls.
Do children pay at DOC campsites?
At many DOC campsites children aged 5 to 17 pay a reduced rate and infants stay free. The fee for each campsite is on its DOC page.

currency.cardText: Reference conversion for trip planning using Reserve Bank of New Zealand rates from {rateDate}. Your bank or card may use another rate and add fees.

Result = amount in NZD × rate of the currency you convert to
currency.formulaNote: Each rate is the number of units of that currency per 1 New Zealand dollar, so every conversion passes through NZD.

assumptions: These are reference rates from {rateDate}. Exchange rates move every day.
Banks, cards and cash machines use their own rates and may add fees, so the amount you pay can differ.
Japanese yen and Korean won are shown without decimals.
faq: What currency is used in New Zealand?
The New Zealand dollar (NZD). Prices in shops, campsites and holiday parks are quoted in NZD.
Is this the rate my bank will give me?
Probably not exactly. This uses reference rates from {rateDate}. Your bank or card provider applies its own rate and fees, so treat the result as a planning figure.

water.metaTitle: Campervan Water Tank Calculator: Fresh and Grey Water Days
water.metaDescription: Work out how many days a campervan's fresh and grey water tanks last for your group, with the formula, a worked example and the daily figures behind it.
water.intro: A tank size in litres only becomes useful once it is days. Enter the fresh and grey water capacity and the number of people to see which tank sets your limit.
water.cardText: Capacity in litres only becomes useful once it is expressed in days. Fresh and grey water are shown separately, because whichever runs out first sets the limit.
formula: Fresh water days = fresh tank (L) ÷ (people × 11 L a day)
Grey water days = grey tank (L) ÷ (people × 9 L a day)
The lower of the two is how long you can stay before refilling or emptying
water.formulaNote: Grey water is the waste from sinks and showers. It is lower than fresh water use because drinking water and cooking water do not all end up in the tank.
water.example: {people} people with a {freshTank} litre fresh tank and a {greyTank} litre grey tank have {freshDays} days of fresh water and {greyDays} days of grey water, so the fresh tank sets the limit.
assumptions: 11 litres of fresh water and 9 litres of grey water per person per day are planning figures for careful use: drinking, cooking, washing up and a quick wash. Showers use far more.
Toilet cassettes and black water are not included.
Empty grey water only at a dump station. Never on the ground or into a stormwater drain.
faq: How long does 100 litres of fresh water last in a campervan?
For two careful users at 11 litres each a day, about four and a half days. Showers and washing clothes shorten that a lot.
Where can I empty grey water in New Zealand?
At a dump station. Many holiday parks have one, and councils run public ones in many towns. Never empty grey water onto the ground or into a stormwater drain.
Which tank runs out first?
Whichever is smaller for your use. Grey tanks are often smaller than fresh tanks, so check both rather than only the fresh water gauge.

doc-huts-new-zealand-guide.title: DOC Huts in New Zealand by Region: Types, Fees, Tickets
doc-huts-new-zealand-guide.description: Where DOC's huts are, region by region, what serviced, standard and basic huts cost in 2026/27, and how hut tickets, the Hut Pass and bookings work.
doc-huts-new-zealand-guide.imageAlt: Backcountry hut in New Zealand mountains
doc-huts-new-zealand-guide.intro: DOC looks after more than 950 huts, and KiwiCamping's DOC data lists 927 of them, from serviced huts with heating and mattresses to two-bunk bivvies. Most sit in the South Island: Canterbury alone has 180 and the West Coast 140, while the North Island's biggest clusters are in the Ruahine, Kaweka and Tararua ranges. In that data, checked on 24 August 2026, only 127 of the 927 could be booked, and although DOC has since moved every serviced hut online, most huts remain first come, first served: free if basic, paid with hut tickets or a Backcountry Hut Pass if standard.

sections.heading: Hut categories and 2026/27 fees
body: Serviced huts have mattresses, a water supply, toilets, handwashing and heating with fuel. For 2026/27 an adult pays $25 a night from May to September, $28 on weeknights and $32 on Friday and Saturday nights from October to April, and $29 and $34 from December to February; children pay half, and camping beside one costs half the hut fee. Standard huts have mattresses, water and toilets, with wood heaters below the bush line, for $15 an adult and $7.50 a child. Basic huts and bivvies are free and offer shelter and little else. In KiwiCamping's data that splits into 96 serviced, 408 standard and 372 basic huts.

Three categories sit outside that ladder. Great Walk huts, 33 of them in KiwiCamping's data, have their own prices by track, season and residency and must be booked in the Great Walks season. Individually priced huts, including serviced alpine huts such as Mueller Hut, set their own fee, and club huts are run by clubs such as the New Zealand Alpine Club, so check the hut's DOC page. Whatever the category, the roof never replaces a sleeping bag, stove, food, head torch and warm layers.
tips: Serviced $25 to $34 by season, standard $15, basic free
Great Walk and alpine huts price individually
Carry full gear whatever the category

sections.heading: Where the huts are, region by region
body: The South Island holds most of the network. Canterbury has 180 huts, led by Lake Sumner Forest Park and Arthur's Pass National Park; the West Coast 140, many up the Whitcombe and Styx valleys; Nelson/Tasman 99, with 45 in Kahurangi National Park and 24 in Nelson Lakes; Otago 78, including 12 in Mount Aspiring National Park and 12 in Hāwea Conservation Park; Southland 70, including 30 on Rakiura; Marlborough 60; and Fiordland 55, almost all inside Fiordland National Park.

In the North Island, Hawke's Bay has 55 huts split between the Kaweka and Ruahine forest parks, Manawatū/Whanganui 43, the East Coast 38 across Te Urewera and Whirinaki, Wairarapa 36 and Wellington/Kāpiti 24, most of them in the Tararua Range. The Central North Island has 16, ten in Tongariro National Park, and Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, Northland, Waikato, Coromandel and Auckland have eight or fewer each.

sections.heading: Hut tickets, passes and bookings
body: Non-bookable huts take Backcountry Hut Tickets, bought before the trip and posted in the honesty box, or a Backcountry Hut Pass that covers most serviced and standard huts for 12 months. From 1 November 2026 hut tickets can also be bought on DOC's online booking system, and paper tickets stay valid until 1 November 2027. Bookable huts are reserved and paid on bookings.doc.govt.nz, and since 1 October 2026 that includes every serviced hut, so Serviced Hut Tickets are being retired.

The common mistake is treating a pass or a ticket as a booking. Neither reserves a bunk or gives priority in a first-come hut. The Hut Pass can pay for some bookable huts if you enter it when booking, but not Great Walk huts in their booking season or the huts on DOC's exclusion list. Read which system the specific hut uses before you leave.
tips: A pass is not a reservation
Hut tickets go online from 1 November 2026
Great Walk huts sell out months ahead

sections.heading: A full hut is still shelter in an emergency
body: At a bookable hut, DOC keeps no space for people without a booking, and you can be turned away when it is full. At non-bookable huts bunks are first come, and the convention is that a full hut means floor space rather than a closed door. Every hut stays open as emergency shelter in bad weather, so do not walk on into darkness because the bunks are taken.

Carry a mat and the means to sleep on the floor, and where the weather allows it and the site permits camping, a tent gives you a genuine alternative. On popular tracks in January, assume the hut will be full and plan accordingly.

sections.heading: Water, cooking and fire
body: Treat hut water unless current DOC information for that hut says it is safe to drink. Roof-collected supply can be contaminated, and giardia is present in New Zealand backcountry water. Boiling is the surest method, and DOC says three minutes; a filter rated for protozoa also works. Assuming is what causes problems.

Cook on your own stove, outside or in the designated area, and never inside a tent. Where a fire is provided, use it sparingly and restock the kindling for whoever arrives next in worse weather than you had.
tips: Treat the water unless told otherwise
Carry a stove regardless
Restock kindling before you leave

sections.heading: Hut etiquette
body: Boots off inside. Keep your gear consolidated on your bunk rather than spread across the table and benches. Be quiet early and move quietly in the morning, because trampers start before dawn and the whole party sleeps in one room after a hard day.
Fill in the hut book, every time, including the date and your intentions. It is a courtesy, and more importantly it can help search and rescue if someone in your party is overdue.

sections.heading: Leaving the hut
body: Sweep the floor, close the shutters and doors properly, and carry out everything you carried in, including food scraps. Rubbish left in a hut attracts rodents, and there is no collection service; whatever you leave stays until another walker removes it.

Report damage, a broken stove, a failed water supply or a hazard to DOC after your trip. Reports help DOC prioritise repairs, and a five-minute message can prevent the next party arriving to a building that does not work.
tips: Carry out all rubbish and scraps
Close shutters and doors
Report damage to DOC afterwards

faq: Do you need to book a DOC hut?

Only some. Great Walk huts, every serviced hut since 1 October 2026 and some popular huts are booked on bookings.doc.govt.nz. Most standard huts are first come, paid with hut tickets or a Backcountry Hut Pass, and basic huts are free.
How much does a DOC hut cost per night?

For 2026/27 a standard hut is $15 for an adult and $7.50 for a child all year. A serviced hut is $25 from May to September and $28 to $34 from October to April, and a basic hut or bivvy is free. Great Walk and individually priced huts set their own fees.

winter-camping-new-zealand.title: Winter camping in New Zealand: warmth, roads and realistic plans
winter-camping-new-zealand.description: Cold nights, short daylight and alpine road controls change how a campervan or tent trip works.
winter-camping-new-zealand.imageAlt: Campervan in a snowy New Zealand landscape
winter-camping-new-zealand.intro: Winter delivers the clearest skies, the emptiest campgrounds and the best value of the year, and it removes most of your margin for error. Cold nights, nine hours of usable daylight, chain controls and seasonal closures are not obstacles to work around afterwards; they are the things the route should be built from.

sections.heading: Rate the sleep system to the night, not the day
body: A bright Central Otago afternoon at fifteen degrees can be followed by a night below zero. Choose a sleeping bag and an insulated mat rated for the overnight minimum in the coldest place you will stop, then add a margin, because comfort ratings are optimistic and a cold night is genuinely miserable.

The mat matters as much as the bag. Most heat is lost downwards into the ground or the vehicle floor, and a summer-weight mat under a good bag will still leave you cold. In a van, insulate the floor and the windows before adding another blanket.
tips: Rate for the overnight low, not the forecast high
Insulated mat beats a warmer bag
Van floors and windows leak heat

sections.heading: Manage condensation
body: Four people breathing in a closed van produce a surprising amount of water, and it ends up in the bedding, the walls and eventually the mattress. Ventilation feels wrong when it is freezing outside, but a permanently sealed vehicle produces wet bedding by the second morning.

Crack a vent or a window on the sheltered side overnight, and air the bedding whenever the sun appears. Wipe condensation off windows in the morning rather than letting it run into the seals and soft furnishings.

sections.heading: Heat the vehicle safely
body: Use installed, manufacturer-approved heating only. Portable gas heaters, camping stoves and barbecues used indoors produce carbon monoxide, which is odourless and has killed people sleeping in vehicles in New Zealand. There is no safe way to improvise cabin heating in a closed space.

If you have a diesel or gas heater fitted, check it works before the trip and know how it vents. A carbon monoxide alarm costs very little and is worth having in any vehicle with a fuel-burning appliance.
tips: Never use a camping stove to heat a van
Carbon monoxide has no smell
Fit a CO alarm if you burn fuel

sections.heading: Chains, tyres and alpine road controls
body: The Lindis Pass, the Crown Range, Arthur's Pass, the Desert Road and the Milford Road can all require chains at short notice, and some rental agreements require you to carry them for the whole trip regardless of forecast. Fitting chains for the first time in sleet on a shoulder is genuinely difficult.

Practise fitting them in a dry driveway in daylight before you leave. Check tyre tread and pressures, confirm the battery is healthy, because cold weather finds a weak one, and read the rental company's winter restrictions before you plan a route over a pass.

sections.heading: Black ice and shaded corners
body: Black ice forms where the road merely looks wet, typically in shade, on bridges, and in the first and last hours of daylight. It gives no warning and no grip, and the standard mistake is braking or steering sharply once you feel it.

Slow down before shaded sections rather than in them, increase following distance well beyond the summer habit, and delay an alpine crossing until the sun has been on the road. Arriving two hours later is not a cost worth arguing about.
tips: Shade and bridges freeze first
Slow before the corner, not in it
Wait for sun on the road

sections.heading: Build the day around the daylight
body: Midwinter gives roughly nine hours of usable light in the south, and less in a valley. That is not much once you have packed camp, driven, stopped and found a site, so plan shorter legs than you would in February and set a firm turnaround time for any walk.

Aim to arrive with light to spare. Choosing a pitch, levelling a vehicle and checking access are all harder in the dark and colder, and a site that would be obviously wrong in daylight is easy to accept at night.

sections.heading: Expect closures and reduced facilities
body: Many DOC campsites close for winter or turn off water, some access roads shut after snow, and holiday parks in small towns can reduce hours or close entirely. A listing written for summer will not tell you this, so check the specific site and the current DOC alerts before committing to it.

Carry more water, food and charge than the plan requires, and treat a cabin or motel night as a normal weather decision rather than a failure. Winter is the season where paying for a room occasionally is what makes the rest of the trip work.
tips: Check the site is open, not just listed
Carry more water than the plan needs
A cabin night is a valid decision

faq: Can you camp in New Zealand in winter?

Yes, and it is the quietest time of year on the road. The limits are practical rather than legal: some DOC campsites and alpine roads close or become chain-only, daylight is short, and a van without insulation or a heater gets unpleasant fast.
Which parts of New Zealand are mildest in winter?

The upper North Island stays the warmest, and Northland and the Coromandel stay campable all year. Central Otago and the Mackenzie country get the hardest frosts, and the West Coast stays mild but very wet.

doc-campsite-rules.title: DOC Campsite Rules 2026: Quiet Hours, Dogs, Drones, Stays
doc-campsite-rules.description: Quiet from 10 pm to 7 am, check-out by 10 am, no pets or drones without DOC permission, and what camping unbooked costs: DOC's terms plus local rules.
doc-campsite-rules.imageAlt: Department of Conservation campsite information board
doc-campsite-rules.intro: Booking a DOC campsite means accepting DOC's booking terms and the local rules on that campsite's own page. The national ones are short: keep noise down from 10 pm to 7 am, check out by 10 am, take all rubbish away, bring no pets or drones unless DOC has authorised them, and do not smoke or vape in huts or toilet blocks. Fires, water, dogs, generators and vehicle access vary by site, so check the site's DOC page and the signs on site.

sections.heading: Use the booking honestly
body: Book the correct date, party and product, then keep confirmation available offline. Where pitches are not individually assigned, choose only from the area available on arrival.

If you miss the first night of a multi-night booking and nobody contacts the site office within 24 hours, DOC cancels the rest with no refund. Do not hold a space with an empty tent or vehicle when nobody intends to stay.

sections.heading: Respect shared hours
body: Standard DOC terms set quiet hours from 10 pm to 7 am unless local rules differ, check-out by 10 am, and check-in between 2 pm and 8.30 pm. Keep generators, music and vehicle movement within the site's limits.
A campsite booking does not guarantee use of a nearby hut's facilities, so plan around the toilets, shelters and water points that come with the campsite.

sections.heading: Leave the site ready
body: Take all rubbish, keep food secure and dispose of grey water only where the site directs. Smoking and vaping are not permitted in huts or toilet blocks.
Pets and drones require explicit permission. Check the exact campsite page rather than treating a quiet location as implied approval.

sections.heading: Booking rules and the unbooked penalty
body: Each campsite page says whether it is bookable or self-registration, and the rules follow from that. At a bookable site you need a valid booking for the night you use it, pass holders included. Without one you have no guaranteed space, and DOC charges its penalty rate: each person pays their normal fee plus a full adult fee, unless they are sheltering in adverse conditions.

At a self-registration site, fill in the form and pay on arrival. Either way, the booking or registration is for the people and vehicle you actually bring, and the confirmation must be available on request, so save it where you can show it without reception.
tips: A pass is not a booking
Unbooked use costs each person their fee plus an adult fee
Register and pay on arrival at first-come sites

sections.heading: Water is often untreated
body: Many DOC sites draw from streams or roof tanks and the supply is not treated. Giardia is present in New Zealand water and a clear stream tells you nothing about it. Boil for at least three minutes, filter, or use chemical treatment, and do not assume a tap is safe because it exists.
Carry enough drinking water to stay independent for a day. Tanks run dry, boil-water notices appear, and a campsite listed as having water can turn out to have a broken supply with no warning.

sections.heading: Generators, drones and dogs
body: Generator rules are set site by site, so check the campsite's DOC page before you run one. Drones require a concession on public conservation land in most circumstances, and even with a DOC permit a drone must keep away from campsites and huts.

DOC's default is no dogs on conservation land unless DOC has approved dog access, and dogs are not allowed in national parks without a permit, to protect kiwi and other ground-nesting birds. In KiwiCamping's DOC data, 207 of the 287 campsites allow no dogs and 74, about a quarter, allow them in some form, mostly on a lead or with a DOC permit. Check the specific site rather than assuming.
tips: Drones need a concession on DOC land
Dogs banned at most DOC sites
Generator rules vary by site

sections.heading: Maximum stay and site conduct
body: Some DOC campsites set a maximum stay on their DOC page to stop long-term occupation, and a Campsite Pass covers no more than 7 nights in any 30 days at one campsite, with extra nights paid at the standard rate. Moving a vehicle a few metres does not reset either limit.

Keep to the marked pitch, do not extend beyond it with awnings or gear where space is tight, and observe quiet hours. These grounds are shared, frequently full, and the enjoyment of everyone depends on people staying within their own space.

sections.heading: Arriving and settling in
body: Turn up in daylight where you can. Choosing a pitch, judging drainage, spotting overhead branches and levelling a vehicle are all considerably harder in the dark, and a site that would obviously be wrong at 4pm is easy to accept at 9pm when you are tired.

Pay on arrival where an honesty box or self-registration applies rather than intending to sort it later. Wardens do check, the fee is small, and the system only works because most people pay without being asked.

Set up within the marked pitch and leave room for whoever arrives after you. At a busy ground in summer, spreading gear across two spaces is the difference between the site holding everyone and people being turned away.

sections.heading: If the campsite is full
body: Popular DOC grounds can be full on summer evenings, so do not count on an overflow area. Creating an extra pitch on the grass, the access lane or beside the toilet block is not an option, and DOC staff can move you on.

Identify a legal fallback before you arrive rather than after. A holiday park half an hour away is a much better outcome than a late drive on an unfamiliar road looking for anywhere that will take you.
tips: Popular grounds fill in summer
Do not count on an overflow area
Know your fallback before arriving

faq: What are the rules at a DOC campsite?

Keep noise down from 10 pm to 7 am, check out by 10 am, take all rubbish away and bring no pets or drones unless DOC has authorised them. Smoking and vaping are banned in huts and toilet blocks, and each site's own page adds rules on fires, dogs, generators and vehicles.
How long can you stay at a DOC campsite?

Some campsites set a maximum stay on their DOC page, and a Campsite Pass covers no more than 7 nights in any 30 days at one campsite. Every night needs a booking or registration except at free basic campsites, and using a bookable site unbooked costs each person their normal fee plus a full adult fee.

doc-hut-rules-etiquette.title: DOC hut rules and backcountry etiquette
doc-hut-rules-etiquette.description: Bookings, bunks, cooking and emergency shelter work differently from ordinary accommodation.
doc-hut-rules-etiquette.imageAlt: Interior of a shared DOC backcountry hut
doc-hut-rules-etiquette.intro: A hut booking buys access to shared shelter, not a private room or a specific bunk unless the product says otherwise. Every person still needs the equipment and judgement to cope if the hut is full, damaged or unreachable.

sections.heading: Carry the right authority
body: Book named huts and dates where reservations apply, or carry the appropriate tickets or pass for non-bookable facilities. Proof should remain available without reception.
Do not rely on unbooked space at a popular hut. Emergency use remains possible in adverse conditions, which is another reason to keep gear compact and considerate.

sections.heading: Live in one room
body: Select an available bunk, keep sleeping gear together and observe quiet hours. Cook only in the designated area, supervise flames and never leave food that attracts rodents.
Use heating fuel conservatively and follow the hut's fire instructions. Wet clothing should not block exits, bunks or the cooking space.

sections.heading: Leave safely
body: Clean benches, sweep where requested, close doors and carry every piece of rubbish out. Treat or boil water according to current advice.
Record intentions with a trusted person and carry navigation and emergency equipment. The hut does not make the track safe or guarantee rescue communication.

sections.heading: Full huts and bookings
body: Bunks in non-bookable huts are first come, and the long convention is that a full hut means floor space rather than a closed door. Bookable huts, including Great Walk huts during the Great Walks season, work differently: you need a booking, and without one you can be turned away. Do not walk on into the dark because the bunks are taken, and equally do not expect someone to give up a bunk they reached first.

Carry a mat so sleeping on the floor is genuinely viable, and where the site permits camping and the weather allows, a tent gives you a real alternative. On popular tracks in summer, plan on the assumption that the hut will be full.
tips: Full hut means floor space
Carry a mat regardless
Assume full in summer

sections.heading: Fill in the hut book, every time
body: The intentions book is one of the first places search and rescue checks when a party is overdue, and an accurate entry has shortened many searches. Record the date, your party, where you came from and where you are going next.
Sign out as well as in where the book allows it. A party recorded as arriving and never leaving generates a search that did not need to happen.

sections.heading: Fire, fuel and cooking
body: Where a hut has a stove, use the firewood sparingly and restock the kindling for whoever arrives next in worse weather than you had. Do not burn rubbish in the hut stove; it damages the flue and leaves the smell for everyone.

Cook on your own stove, in the designated area or outside, never in a tent or a confined porch. Carry enough fuel for the trip plus a margin, because there is nothing available at a hut and a borrowed stove is an imposition.
tips: Restock kindling before leaving
Never burn rubbish in the stove
Carry your own stove and fuel

sections.heading: Leaving it better than you found it
body: Sweep, close the shutters and door catches properly against wind and rodents, and carry out everything you carried in including food scraps. There is no rubbish collection at a backcountry hut, so whatever you leave stays until another walker removes it.

Report damage, a failed water supply or a hazard to DOC after the trip. Maintenance is prioritised on what gets reported, and a short message can stop the next party arriving to a building that does not work.

sections.heading: Sharing a hut with strangers
body: A backcountry hut puts a dozen people who have never met into one room after a hard day. Almost all of the etiquette follows from that: keep your gear in your own space, do not run a stove or a bright light in someone's face, and accept that somebody will snore.

Offer space on the bench and the bunks rather than waiting to be asked. Parties arriving late are usually wet and cold, and the difference between a welcoming hut and a miserable one is entirely down to whoever got there first.
Head torches on red mode after dark, and pack your bag in the porch if you are leaving before the others. Rustling a dry bag at 5am is one of the commonest complaints in New Zealand huts.

sections.heading: Booking seasons and what changes
body: Great Walk huts run a booked season with higher fees, wardens and full facilities, then revert to a lower standard and price outside it. Gas, heating and sometimes the water supply are removed in the off season.
Check what the hut actually offers for your dates rather than the summer description. An off-season Great Walk hut can be considerably colder and barer than the photographs suggest.
tips: Facilities drop outside the season
Gas and heating may be removed
Check the hut for your actual dates

faq: Can you be turned away from a full DOC hut?

On a bookable hut, yes: a bunk is only yours if you booked it. On a first-come hut nobody can be turned out, which is exactly why the etiquette matters and why you should always carry a tent or bivvy on a popular track.
What are you expected to do before leaving a hut?

Sweep the floor, replace any firewood you burned, take every piece of rubbish with you and fill in the hut book. The hut book entry matters beyond courtesy, because it is what search and rescue reads if someone is reported overdue.
